scope: Build/test classpath only, absent from all63 deployed runtime jars. Preconnection boundary rejects remote transports/configuration before SDK resource allocation, and pins one canonical local Unix socket. The real 104-test suite includes10 separate-process rejection cases plus original strict94.
observedImplementation: Primary vendor source plus actual shaded bytecode construct classic CloseableHttpClient, classic connection manager and executeOpen(ClassicHttpRequest/Response). Unix-scheme socket factory invokes UnixSocket.get(canonical path). HttpCore H2 is bundled, but observed classic HTTP/1 API path does not invoke HPACK. This is bounded path inspection, not whole-JVM exploit/callgraph proof.

findings.classification: HTTP/1 response parsing exists and could be affected by malicious local daemon; remote attacker transport rejected. Keep residual local daemon trust, do not claim NOT AFFECTED.
HTTP/2 HPACK exists in shaded archive; actual Docker transport uses classic HTTP/1 path, no HPACK observed. No universal unreachable-code proof.
Classic client path is used and content compression is not disabled; malformed Content-Encoding could leak a local-daemon connection. Same trusted-local mitigation, not absence-of-feature.

remediation: Vendor remains latest3.7.1 with embedded shaded old classes. Maven overrides cannot replace shaded bytes; no unsupported byte patch applied. Reassess when vendor updates, or before any remote/untrusted Docker use.
